sources: NASTE (National Association of Summer STEM Training Experiences)
metadata._verificationNotes: Data integrity enforced on 2026-04-23. 82 verified, 744 non-verified, 71 dupes removed.
metadata._formatBackfillNotes: Backfilled format for 744 entries based on location.state. Online→online, Remote→remote, all others→in-person.

programs.name: Pacific Science Center Camps for Curious Minds
programs.description: Over 100 unique STEAM camp experiences across six Seattle-area locations for PreK-8. Themes include robotics, dissection lab, environmental engineering, and more. Sensory-friendly and girls-focused options available. Scholarships cover registration, lunches, and afternoon care through the Access to Science Pipeline.

programs.name: Museum of Flight ACE (Aerospace Camp Experience)
programs.description: Week-long aerospace camps at the Museum of Flight in Seattle for K-9th graders. Hands-on activities in aviation and space including group projects, experiments, visits from aerospace professionals, and museum exhibit exploration. Runs June 22 through August 28, 2026.

programs.name: DigiPen Open World Summer Workshops (Ages 5-12)
programs.description: Hands-on STEAM workshops at DigiPen's Redmond campus for ages 5-12 covering game design, programming, robotics, art, and animation. Age-appropriate tracks tailored to 5-9 and 10-12 age groups. Girls-focused STEM tracks also available.

programs.name: Seattle MESA (Mathematics, Engineering, Science Achievement)
programs.description: Year-round STEM enrichment for grades 6-12 with after-school tutoring, statewide STEM competitions, mentorship, and a 3-week summer math scholars program for incoming freshmen. Emphasis on traditionally underrepresented students in STEM fields. MESA periods during the school day let advisors work with students on academics.

programs.name: UW Engineering Discovery Days
programs.provider: University of Washington College of Engineering
programs.description: Annual 2-day spring event oriented toward 4th-8th grade students that draws up to 10,000 visitors to UW campus. UW engineering students and faculty share their work through hands-on activities, introducing students to engineering disciplines and research.

programs.name: UW Engineering Academy
programs.provider: University of Washington College of Engineering
programs.description: Free one-week summer program at UW Seattle preparing Washington state students for engineering careers. July 20-24, 2026, 10AM-4PM. Must be a rising 10th or 11th grader attending high school in the greater Seattle area.

programs.name: UW Changemakers in Computing (CiC)
programs.provider: University of Washington Paul G. Allen School
programs.description: Free summer program for rising juniors and seniors at Washington state high schools. Develop coding skills through culturally relevant, project-based learning, explore areas of computing, and discover changemaking impact through technology.

programs.name: Museum of Flight Aeronautical Explorations
programs.description: Free formal credit-bearing CTE summer school course for rising 9th-12th graders. June 29 - July 17, 2026, 8:30AM-3:30PM M-F. Earn 0.5 high school CTE credits. Includes graded tests, quizzes, and projects equivalent to a semester course. Must be a WA state resident.

programs.name: DigiPen WANIC Summer Programs
programs.description: Free state-funded 3-week program at DigiPen's Redmond campus. June 29 - July 17, 2026, 8AM-3PM M-F. Covers game design, programming, digital art, and animation. No tuition or fees.

programs.name: Robinson Center Saturday Enrichment Program
programs.provider: UW Robinson Center for Young Scholars
programs.description: Saturday enrichment courses at UW for academically advanced students. Offerings span STEM, humanities, and creative arts. Hosted at the UW Guggenheim Annex. Spring 2026 offerings available with registration opening in March.

programs.name: UW Youth & Teen Programs
programs.description: Remote and in-person enrichment courses for teens in coding, data visualization, writing, and more. Four sessions offered throughout the year. Summer 2026 courses available.

programs.name: Washington MESA College Prep Program
programs.provider: University of Washington Office of Minority Affairs
programs.description: Statewide program with centers across Washington engaging middle and high school students in STEM through after-school tutoring, competitions, mentorship. Emphasis on underrepresented students. Summer math scholars program for incoming freshmen.

programs.name: Destination Science Summer Camps — Seattle
programs.description: Week-long in-person STEM camps across the Seattle area with hands-on science projects. Multiple 2026 themes available. Focuses on experiential learning in science for elementary students.

programs.name: Rice University STEM-Letics Academy
programs.description: Week-long summer academy at Rice University for 3rd-5th graders combining STEM and physical activities to keep students mentally and physically active. Offered multiple weeks during summer.

programs.name: Camp Invention — Texas Locations
programs.description: Nationally recognized summer day camp with hands-on STEM adventures led by local educators. Held at schools and community centers across Texas. Activities designed by National Inventors Hall of Fame inductees.

programs.name: Rice Bio Academies
programs.description: Immersive hands-on summer experience at Rice University for 7th-11th graders offered in three focused sections: BioTech, BioMed, and BioEng. Students work in Rice research labs alongside faculty.

programs.name: Houston PREP (Prefreshman Enrichment Program)
programs.description: Free summer enrichment for grades 6-12 aimed at enhancing academic backgrounds of socially and economically disadvantaged students in STEM. Long-running Houston program.

programs.name: Girls Inc. Dallas Eureka! STEM Program
programs.description: Free STEM enrichment program for 7th-8th grade girls in the Dallas metro area. Multi-year program with summer intensive and year-round activities exploring science, technology, engineering, and math careers.

programs.name: Governor's Summer Merit Program — Texas
programs.description: State-sponsored summer camp motivating Texas high school students to consider STEM careers. Students explore multiple STEM fields and are introduced to in-demand skilled STEM jobs.

programs.name: LA's BEST Summer Learning Program
programs.description: Free full-day summer enrichment at select LAUSD elementary schools. Keeps children safe, healthy, and learning all summer with STEAM activities, field trips, and recreation. Runs several weeks in June and July.

programs.name: Club SciKidz Silicon Valley
programs.description: Hands-on STEM summer camps in Silicon Valley with experiments and interactive projects. Curriculum designed to inspire a love of science, technology, and engineering in young learners.

programs.name: COSMOS (CA State Summer School for Math & Science)
programs.description: Prestigious free residential summer program at six UC campuses (Davis, Irvine, LA, Merced, San Diego, Santa Cruz). Students explore STEM topics, work with renowned faculty, and conduct research in state-of-the-art facilities. Grades 8-12.

programs.name: SAGE (Science Accelerating Girls' Engagement in STEM)
programs.description: Free one-week residential camp for Northern California public school students. Students make professional connections, learn about scientific discoveries and engineering, and explore STEM careers. Open to freshmen through juniors.

programs.name: Camp CHLA (Children's Hospital Los Angeles)
programs.description: Free 5-day immersive healthcare exploration at Children's Hospital LA for LA County freshmen-juniors. Meet medical professionals, observe clinical settings, and gain firsthand healthcare experience.

programs.name: CYC Summer Programs (Community Youth Center SF)
programs.provider: Community Youth Center of San Francisco
programs.description: Free summer program with weekly field trips and hands-on, age-appropriate curriculum integrating literacy, math, STEAM, and recreation. Supports students academically, socially, and emotionally.

programs.name: Summer Rising 2026
programs.description: Free citywide summer learning and enrichment for K-8 students in NYC. Teacher-led ELA and math instruction, plus enrichment in STEM, arts, financial literacy, sports, and field trips. Elementary runs 7 weeks (Jul 1 - Aug 14), middle school runs 6 weeks (Jul 1 - Aug 7).

programs.name: STEM Matters NYC Enrichment Programs
programs.provider: NYC Department of Education / Cultural Institutions
programs.description: Free summer enrichment at cultural institutions across all five NYC boroughs. One-week camps and multi-week high school programs for grades 1-12 in NYC public and charter schools. Spring and summer break programming.

programs.name: Cooper Union Summer STEM 2026
programs.description: Free 6-week in-person STEM program at Cooper Union (July 6 - Aug 13, 2026, M-Th 9AM-3PM). Open to high school students worldwide with priority for NYC residents. Rigorous engineering and science curriculum at 41 Cooper Square.

programs.name: Columbia University S-PREP (State Pre-College Enrichment)
programs.description: Free high school and college preparatory program for students interested in medicine or related STEM fields. Includes both summer and academic year sessions at Columbia University. Strong pathway for pre-med students.

programs.name: Columbia Double Discovery Center Summer Academy
programs.description: Free 4-week academic enrichment commuter program at Columbia University for 9th-10th graders in NYC. Immersive college campus experience with courses in reading, writing, and research skills.

programs.name: New York Edge Summer Camp
programs.description: Free summer program offering STEM, arts, sports, and academic enrichment to NYC public school students. Community-based programming at schools across the city.

programs.name: Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum Summer Camps
programs.description: Hands-on science summer camps for K-8 at the Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum. Students explore robotics, forensics, flight, and more through experiential science education.

programs.name: Henry Ford Summer Camps
programs.description: Summer camps at The Henry Ford for grades 2-7 featuring artifact explorations and unique learning experiences. June 15 - Aug 28, 2026. Students explore innovation, invention, and American ingenuity through hands-on activities.

programs.name: Michigan Science Center Summer Camps
programs.description: STEM summer camps at the Michigan Science Center in Detroit exploring earth science, animals, engineering, LEGO building, and astronaut skills. Hands-on experiments and interactive learning.

programs.name: Michigan Tech Summer Youth Programs
programs.description: Week-long residential and day camps at Michigan Tech covering engineering, science, computing, and outdoor adventures. Middle and high school programs available. Students explore STEM disciplines on a university campus.

programs.name: EMU Engage K-12 Camp Programs
programs.description: Range of academic and STEM summer camps at Eastern Michigan University for K-12 students. Programs include science, technology, arts, and enrichment activities on the EMU campus.

programs.name: NYLF Explore STEM (Middle School)
programs.description: Week-long residential STEM program for middle schoolers at university campuses including Loyola, University of Miami, Villanova, UT Dallas, Rice, and UC San Diego. Hands-on activities: coding robots, solving crime scenes, dissecting lungs. Connect with industry professionals.

programs.name: NSLC (National Student Leadership Conference)
programs.description: 30 different pre-college career exploration programs across 13 university campuses. Programs run 6, 9, or 18 days covering medicine, engineering, law, business, and more. Since 1989, NSLC has been a leading provider of experiential learning for high schoolers.

programs.name: Camp Invention (National)
programs.description: Nationally recognized STEM day camp with hands-on invention activities at 1,500+ school and community locations. Curriculum designed by National Inventors Hall of Fame inductees. Led by local certified educators.

programs.name: NYLF Pathways to STEM (Elementary)
programs.description: Residential STEM experience for elementary students (grades 3-5) introducing pathways in science, technology, engineering, and math through hands-on experiments, team challenges, and college campus exploration.

programs.name: Washington STEM Network Programs
programs.description: Statewide nonprofit connecting students, schools, and communities to STEM opportunities across Washington. Regional STEM networks coordinate local programs, resources, and career-connected learning from elementary through high school.

programs.name: Seattle Public Schools Expanded Learning Summer
programs.description: Free full-day summer program providing targeted academic support and enrichment five days per week. Available to SPS students, with priority for students scoring below 60th percentile in Math and Reading.

programs.name: Seattle University AI for Equity Pre-College Program
programs.description: Pre-college residential program exploring the intersection of AI and criminal justice. Students examine modern technology issues like bias, equity, and AI ethics. Runs July 12-17, 2026 as an overnight program. College credit available. Merit scholarships offered for students with financial need.

programs.name: Seattle University Summer Business Institute
programs.description: Credit-bearing residential summer business program for high school students. Explore various business disciplines through experiential learning. Students live on-campus July 19-25, 2026. Includes interactions with Seattle business leaders and entrepreneurs.

programs.name: Summer@Cornish Art & Design Intensive
programs.provider: Cornish College of the Arts / Seattle University
programs.description: 4-week intensive pre-college arts program at Cornish College in Seattle's South Lake Union. Choose from art & design, music, film, musical theater, or dance. Full-day and half-day options with optional on-campus housing. Afternoons feature cross-disciplinary electives.

programs.name: Lakeside Summer Institute: AI & Machine Learning
programs.description: Lakeside Summer Institute courses offer students the opportunity to learn from experts in AI, molecular biology, and planetary science, gaining real-world skills. Also includes competition math (AMC prep) and environmental solutions courses. Financial aid available on first-come basis.

programs.name: UW Youth & Teen Engineering Challenges
programs.description: Summer engineering courses on the UW Seattle campus for high school students. Over 100 courses available including Introduction to Engineering Design & Process and hands-on Engineering Challenges. In-person and online options available.

programs.name: Lakeside Educational Enrichment Program (LEEP)
programs.description: Free 4-week summer enrichment program at Lakeside School for current 5th and 8th graders in Seattle Public Schools entering 6th or 9th grade. Includes classes, sports, outdoor activities, trips, and field days. Free daily bus transportation within Seattle city limits. July 6-31, 2026.

programs.name: Washington Aerospace Scholars (WAS)
programs.description: Two-phase program for WA state high school juniors: online UW college course on aerospace design and NASA space exploration (earns 5 UW credits), followed by a 6-day summer residency at the Museum of Flight. Work with STEM professionals, NASA scientists, and university students.

programs.name: ACAP Seattle Residency Week
programs.description: Free week-long residential program at UW for WA high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors underrepresented in accounting. Immersed in the college experience: stay on UW campus, learn about accounting and business majors, visit firms, and get matched with a year-long mentor.

programs.name: UW Changemakers in Computing
programs.description: Free 4-week in-person summer program at UW Seattle for WA state high school juniors and seniors with little to no prior computing experience. July 6-30, 2026. Introduction to computing concepts, hands-on projects, and exposure to tech careers.

programs.name: Seattle University Urban Sustainability Pre-College Program
programs.description: Overnight pre-college program at Seattle University incorporating biology, chemistry, environmental studies, and environmental engineering with emphasis on social equity and environmental justice. Activities include urban wildlife camera trapping, fish counting and identification, and water sampling.

programs.name: UW STEP (Students Exploring Pharmacy)
programs.provider: University of Washington School of Pharmacy
programs.description: 4-day program at UW School of Pharmacy for grades 9-12. Interactive presentations, labs, discussion groups, tours, and workshops including basic medication compounding, exploring treatment approaches, medication safety and quality, and practicing clinical skills.

programs.name: Lakeside Summer Institute: Science Courses
programs.description: Advanced science courses at Lakeside School covering AI, molecular biology, and planetary science. Students learn from experts in each field, gaining real-world skills. Lakeside is one of Seattle's most prestigious private schools.

programs.name: DigiPen Academy Pre-College Summer Programs
programs.description: 4-week pre-college summer program in Art & Animation for Games, Game Design, Game Programming, or Music & Sound Design for Games. Students work together to create a game from start to finish. Classes M-F 9:30am-4:30pm PST. Must be entering junior/senior year or graduated within 18 months.

programs.name: UW Changemakers in Computing Summer 2026
programs.description: Free in-person summer program for WA state high school juniors and seniors with little to no prior computing experience. Runs July 6-30 M-Th on UW Seattle campus. Designed for students from underrepresented backgrounds and economically disadvantaged families.

programs.name: UW Students Exploring Pharmacy (STEP)
programs.provider: University of Washington School of Pharmacy
programs.description: Free 4-day in-person program for grades 9-12 interested in pharmacy, healthcare, or STEM careers. Hands-on learning, small-group activities, and direct interaction with UW faculty, pharmacy students, and pharmacists.

programs.name: Girls Who Code Pathways Program
programs.description: Free 7-week virtual summer program for high school girls and non-binary students. Learn AI, data science, cybersecurity, game design, or web development through hands-on projects. Self-paced asynchronous format with optional live events, mentorship, and peer collaboration via private Discord. No prior coding experience required.

programs.name: Johns Hopkins Center for Talented Youth (CTY) On-Campus
programs.description: Prestigious residential program for academically talented students. Three-week intensive courses in STEM, humanities, writing, debate, and engineering. Students live on a college campus, participate in evening activities and field trips. Talent-identified students through qualifying test scores. One of the most recognized gifted programs in the country.

programs.name: Stanford Pre-Collegiate Summer Institutes
programs.description: Two-week intensive online courses taught by Stanford instructors. Over 75 subjects including Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Creative Writing, Philosophy, Mathematics. Daily synchronous classes with rigorous academics. Ungraded, no college credit, but Stanford certificate of completion. Financial aid available based on demonstrated need.
programs.duration: 2 weeks (Session I: June 15-26, Session II: July 6-17)

programs.name: LaunchX Online Entrepreneurship Program
programs.description: 5-week online entrepreneurship program where students develop real business ideas, create prototypes, pitch to mentors, and collaborate with peers from 60+ countries. Mentorship from MIT-trained entrepreneurs. Students build business plans and functional prototypes. Financial awards available for applicants who apply by February 11.

programs.name: Interlochen Arts Camp
programs.description: One of the nation's premier summer arts programs. 1-6 week residential sessions in music, visual arts, dance, theatre, and creative writing. Study with professional artists, perform in concerts and exhibitions. Camp activities include lakeside recreation. 85% of financial aid applicants receive assistance. Audition/portfolio-based merit scholarships available.

programs.name: Boston University Tanglewood Institute (BUTI) Young Artists
programs.description: Highly selective residential music program at the Tanglewood Music Festival. Young Artists Orchestra, Wind Ensemble, and specialized tracks (harp, voice). Study with professional conductors and musicians. Perform at one of the most prestigious music festivals in the world. Master classes, rehearsals, and performances in a concert-quality setting.

programs.name: UW Center for Neurotechnology YSP-REACH
programs.provider: University of Washington Center for Neurotechnology
programs.description: Five-day summer program at UW for high school students interested in STEM careers, with a focus on neural engineering and neuroscience. Students explore brain-computer interfaces, neuroprosthetics, and computational neuroscience through hands-on labs and faculty-led sessions.

programs.name: Gonzaga SEAS Summer Immersion Program (SSIP)
programs.description: Introduces high school students interested in math and science to college life and careers in engineering and computer science. Includes hands-on projects, campus tours, and mentorship from Gonzaga engineering faculty and students. Free residential program for Pacific Northwest students.

programs.name: Rice Tapia STEM Camps
programs.description: 6-day/5-night residential STEM camp at Rice University in Houston. Multiple sessions July 5-24, 2026. Students explore coding, robotics, data science, and engineering through hands-on projects and labs. Meals and lodging included. Named after Rice mathematician Richard Tapia.

programs.name: Columbia SHAPE — Summer High School Academic Program for Engineers
programs.description: Free 3-week intensive engineering program at Columbia University for NYC-area high school students from underrepresented backgrounds. Students work on real engineering projects in biomedical, chemical, civil, computer science, electrical, and mechanical engineering labs. Includes mentorship and college readiness workshops.

programs.name: Texas Tech Clark Scholars Program
programs.description: Prestigious 7-week summer research program selecting only 12 rising seniors nationwide. Students work one-on-one with Texas Tech faculty mentors on independent research projects across sciences, humanities, engineering, and social sciences. Includes $750 stipend, housing, and meal plan. One of the most selective HS research programs in the country.

programs.name: Columbia Double Discovery Center Pre-College Program
programs.description: Free summer and year-round academic enrichment for first-generation and low-income NYC high school students. Includes SAT prep, college counseling, academic tutoring, cultural enrichment trips, and campus-based programming at Columbia. Serves 700+ students annually since 1965.

programs.name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
programs.description: Highly competitive 8-week summer research program at Stanford Med for rising juniors and seniors from the San Francisco Bay Area. Students conduct mentored research in biomedical sciences including genetics, immunology, neuroscience, and oncology. Free with potential stipends up to $3,000. Priority for first-gen and underrepresented students.

programs.name: UW Center for Neurotechnology Summer Research (YSP-REACH)
programs.description: High school students explore neural engineering and neuroscience at UW's Center for Neurotechnology. Tour labs, learn about brain-computer interfaces, and get introduced to neuroengineering. Stipend included. Strong pipeline for college applications in neuroscience and bioengineering.

programs.name: UW Materials Science Camp for High Schoolers
programs.description: Week-long materials science camp at UW's Materials Science & Engineering department. Students explore polymers, metals, ceramics, and composites through hands-on lab activities. Learn about real-world applications in aerospace, biomedical, and sustainable materials.

programs.name: NASA STEM Enhancement in Earth Science (SEES)
programs.provider: NASA / UT Austin Center for Space Research
programs.description: Two-week NASA-funded on-site internship at UT Austin for rising juniors/seniors. Collaborate with NASA scientists and academic experts on Earth science research including astronomy, planetary science, remote sensing, and space geodesy. Must be 16 by program start and a US citizen.

programs.name: NSLC Pre-College Career Programs
programs.description: Pre-college leadership programs in Medicine, Business, STEM, Law, Intelligence, and more. Held at top universities including Georgetown, American University, and Georgia Tech. Students engage in hands-on simulations, site visits, and mentorship with professionals.

programs.name: Anson L. Clark Scholars Program
programs.description: Highly competitive 7-week summer research program at Texas Tech. 12 scholars per year work one-on-one with faculty on original research in sciences, engineering, humanities, and social sciences. Includes $750 stipend, room and board, and weekly seminars with visiting scholars.

programs.name: MIT MITES (MOSTEC)
programs.description: Immerse yourself in a 6-week residential engineering experience at MIT designed specifically for high-achieving minority and first-generation students. Work in state-of-the-art labs, collaborate with peers from across the country, and receive mentoring from MIT students and faculty. Develop technical skills, build lasting professional networks, and gain confidence in your ability to succeed in rigorous STEM environments.
programs.advisorNote: MITES is one of the most prestigious pathways for underrepresented students in STEM—admission demonstrates exceptional potential and commitment. Colleges view this program as a strong signal of both academic excellence and diversity contribution.

programs.name: Stanford Summer Research College (SIMR)
programs.description: Spend 8 weeks conducting original research at Stanford across engineering, computer science, chemistry, and biology. Work directly with PhD graduate students and faculty mentors on real projects, participate in seminars, and present your findings. Gain deep lab experience, understand graduate-level research workflows, and build relationships with researchers in your field of interest.
programs.advisorNote: SIMR provides genuine research experience that directly strengthens STEM college applications—especially valuable if you choose a project you can discuss in detail during interviews. The research credential carries weight with top universities.

programs.name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
programs.description: Attend a highly selective 4-week summer program bringing together exceptional STEM students from around the world. Dive deep into advanced physics, computer science, or mathematics through intensive coursework and research projects. Experience dorm life with international peers, attend seminars from leading scientists, and work on problems that push the boundaries of these fields.
programs.advisorNote: RSI's global reputation and rigorous curriculum make it exceptionally valuable for STEM applications. Colleges recognize the program's selectivity—admission itself becomes a talking point in your application narrative.

programs.name: COSMOS (California State Summer School for Mathematics & Science)
programs.description: Spend 4 weeks at a UC campus (Davis, Irvine, or Santa Cruz) exploring specialized STEM topics through daily lectures, hands-on labs, and field trips. Choose a cluster matching your interests and work alongside peers with similar passions. Engage in project-based learning, interact with UC faculty, and experience university-level coursework while living on campus.
programs.advisorNote: COSMOS is an excellent option for California students seeking affordable, quality STEM enrichment. While less selective than MIT MITES or RSI, it still demonstrates serious interest in STEM and provides solid research foundations.

programs.name: PROMYS (Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists)
programs.description: Explore pure mathematics over 6 weeks through a residential program emphasizing mathematical proof and problem-solving. Investigate deep topics in number theory, abstract algebra, and combinatorics. Study alongside gifted young mathematicians, learn from university faculty, and develop the kind of rigorous mathematical thinking valued in higher mathematics.
programs.advisorNote: PROMYS is the go-to program for students serious about advanced mathematics—colleges view it as strong evidence of mathematical maturity. Ideal if you're considering math, physics, or computer science at selective universities.

programs.name: HCSSiM (Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics)
programs.description: 6-week intensive summer math program. Advanced topics in discrete math, algebra, topology. Highly collaborative environment with daily problem sets and lectures.
programs.advisorNote: STEM-focused programs show serious interest in your field. Be specific about technical skills you gained and how they advanced your understanding.

programs.name: SUMaC (Stanford University Mathematics Camp)
programs.description: 5-week residential mathematics program featuring advanced topics in algebra, topology, and combinatorics. Lectures by Stanford faculty and postdocs. Develop hands-on skills, work with peers who share your interests, and gain insight into this field's real-world applications.
programs.advisorNote: STEM programs demonstrate commitment to your major. Be ready to discuss specific technical skills or concepts you mastered.

programs.name: Ross Mathematics Program
programs.description: 6-week residential summer program emphasizing mathematical proof and number theory. Problem-solving focused with peer mentoring and evening colloquia.
programs.advisorNote: STEM-focused programs show serious interest in your field. Be specific about technical skills you gained and how they advanced your understanding.

programs.name: Garcia MRSEC Summer Camp
programs.description: 6-week summer research camp introducing high school students to materials science and engineering. Laboratory experience with Columbia faculty. Develop hands-on skills, work with peers who share your interests, and gain insight into this field's real-world applications.
programs.advisorNote: Research experience strengthens STEM applications and demonstrates genuine interest in your field. Document what you learned.

programs.name: Clark Scholar Program
programs.description: An intensive 7-week summer research program where students work one-on-one with mentors on original biology and life sciences research projects. Based at the University of Pennsylvania, the program combines hands-on lab work, scientific writing, and professional development. Engage in real research that contributes to published work, mentored by active researchers.
programs.advisorNote: The Clark Program offers substantial research experience with publication potential—a major advantage for pre-med and life sciences students. The one-on-one mentorship and original research contribution strengthen medical school and graduate school applications significantly.

programs.name: Harvard Summer School for High School Students
programs.description: Take college-level courses during Harvard's summer session, experiencing authentic university learning in subjects ranging from STEM to humanities. Attend lectures from Harvard faculty, study in university libraries, and engage in rigorous academics in Harvard's historic academic environment. Options for both day and residential students.
programs.advisorNote: Harvard Summer School provides institutional access and a college transcript—useful for demonstrating ability to handle college coursework. However, admissions committees typically view this differently than more selective, competitive summer programs.

programs.name: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS)
programs.description: 2-week residential program focused on global citizenship and leadership. Guest lectures, seminars on international affairs, and overnight trips to major cities.
programs.advisorNote: Leadership programs demonstrate initiative and ability to influence others—colleges value students who take on substantial roles. Use this to show your unique contributions.

programs.name: Columbia Summer High School Program
programs.description: Take college-level courses at Columbia for high school credit. Multiple sessions during summer. Access to Columbia library and campus facilities. Gain valuable experience, network with peers, and develop skills relevant to your academic and career goals.
programs.advisorNote: Emphasize specific skills you developed and how this experience shaped your perspective on your chosen field.

programs.name: Penn Summer High School Program
programs.description: Attend UPenn college courses. STEM and liberal arts offerings. Gain college credit and experience university life. Gain valuable experience, network with peers, and develop skills relevant to your academic and career goals.
programs.advisorNote: Emphasize specific skills you developed and how this experience shaped your perspective on your chosen field.

programs.name: Princeton Summer School
programs.description: Selective summer program at Princeton. College-level courses in STEM and humanities. Residential experience at elite institution. Gain valuable experience, network with peers, and develop skills relevant to your academic and career goals.
programs.advisorNote: Emphasize specific skills you developed and how this experience shaped your perspective on your chosen field.

programs.name: Brown Pre-College Program
programs.description: Multi-week summer program taking Brown college courses. Day and residential options. Access to Brown facilities and mentorship. Gain valuable experience, network with peers, and develop skills relevant to your academic and career goals.
programs.advisorNote: Emphasize specific skills you developed and how this experience shaped your perspective on your chosen field.

programs.name: Cornell Summer College
programs.description: Attend Cornell college courses for credit. Multiple 2-6 week sessions. Engineering, arts, sciences offerings. Residential campus experience. Gain valuable experience, network with peers, and develop skills relevant to your academic and career goals.
programs.advisorNote: Emphasize specific skills you developed and how this experience shaped your perspective on your chosen field.

programs.name: HOBY (Hugh O'Brien Youth Leadership)
programs.description: Leadership seminar program with state conferences and alumni programs. Focus on personal development, character development, and community service. Build leadership capacity through workshops, team challenges, and mentoring from experienced leaders in your community.
programs.advisorNote: Leadership involvement shows initiative and character—colleges value students who step up. Highlight your specific contributions and growth.

programs.name: Boys & Girls State Programs
programs.description: Week-long summer civics program. Mock state government with elected offices. Leadership, citizenship, and government education. Build leadership capacity through workshops, team challenges, and mentoring from experienced leaders in your community.
programs.advisorNote: Leadership involvement shows initiative and character—colleges value students who step up. Highlight your specific contributions and growth.

programs.name: National Student Leadership Conference (NSLC)
programs.description: Leadership development programs held in major U.S. cities. Focus on public speaking, teamwork, and personal leadership. Week-long residential experience.
programs.advisorNote: Leadership programs demonstrate initiative and ability to influence others—colleges value students who take on substantial roles. Use this to show your unique contributions.

programs.name: Bank of America Student Leaders
programs.description: Year-round leadership program. Community service focus. Local chapter participation with mentoring from banking professionals. Build leadership capacity through workshops, team challenges, and mentoring from experienced leaders in your community.
programs.advisorNote: Leadership involvement shows initiative and character—colleges value students who step up. Highlight your specific contributions and growth.

programs.name: Congressional Award Program
programs.description: Develop leadership skills and civic awareness through the Congressional Award Program program. Meet other ambitious young leaders from your state and across the nation. programs.name: Burke Museum Summer Camps (Dino Trackers & Paleo Discovery)
programs.provider: Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (UW)

Paleo Discovery serves grades 4-6 with a closer look at Burke paleontology collections including fossils, dig pits, and Burke educator-led investigations. programs.name: YMCA Camp Orkila Overnight Summer Camp

cost.display: Sliding scale — Price A (full) / Price B (subsidized); $50 deposit; financial assistance available

programs.deadline: Registration opens February 4, 2026 at 6 a.m.; sessions fill quickly
programs.description: Residential overnight camp on the northwest tip of Orcas Island, operating since 1906. Programs for kids and teens entering grades 3-12 in sessions of 7-28 days, grouped by grade and gender identity in fully-enclosed cabins. Activities include archery, boating, climbing wall, zipline, challenge course, marine science, arts & crafts, and traditional camp programs. Sliding-scale pricing (Price A/B) plus need-based financial assistance keep camp accessible.
programs.dates: Sessions late June through late August 2026 (e.g., Session 2A Jul 13-24, Session 6A Aug 10-21)
programs.scholarshipAid: Available — sliding scale + need-based financial assistance
programs.howToStart: Registration opens Feb 4, 2026 at 6 a.m.; create account at seattleymca.org and apply for financial assistance separately if needed.

programs.name: Camp Sealth Overnight & Day Camp

cost.display: Varies by session — see registration page

programs.dates: 8 sessions, late June through end of August 2026

programs.name: Woodland Park Zoo Summer Day Camps

cost.display: Varies by age tier and session — see registration page

programs.deadline: Rolling — popular sessions fill in spring
programs.description: Themed day camps for kids ages 4–13 at Woodland Park Zoo in Seattle. Camps are tiered by age with developmentally appropriate, NGSS-aligned curricula focused on animals, ecosystems and biology — campers get hands-on activities and zoo encounters. Preschool through kindergarten attend two- or three-day camps; first grade and up attend four- and five-day camps. Partial and full scholarships available in 20% increments up to 100% for families with financial barriers.
programs.dates: Summer 2026 — multiple sessions across the season
programs.scholarshipAid: Available — partial and full (up to 100%) for qualifying families
programs.howToStart: Register at zoo.org/camps; popular sessions fill in spring. Apply for scholarships during registration.

programs.name: Seattle Aquarium Marine Summer Camp
programs.deadline: Rolling — registration is open
programs.description: The Seattle Aquarium's Marine Summer Camp serves children ages 6–12 at the Aquarium on Pier 59. Campers explore Puget Sound marine life through guided behind-the-scenes activities, exhibit time, hands-on labs and group play. Camp groups are placed by age tier so curricula match developmental stage. Before and after care available 8:30–9:15am and 4–4:45pm for an additional fee. A limited number of needs-based scholarships are offered. Note: per-session tuition not posted on the public landing page; confirm directly via registration@seattleaquarium.org.
programs.dates: Summer 2026 — multiple weeklong sessions
programs.scholarshipAid: Available — limited number of needs-based scholarships
programs.howToStart: Register at seattleaquarium.org/explore-the-aquarium/programs/marine-summer-camp; email registration@seattleaquarium.org for tuition specifics or scholarship application.

programs.name: Seattle Children's Theatre Drama School Summer Camps

cost.display: Varies by camp — see 2026 Summer Digital Course Catalog

programs.name: Outschool Online Summer Camps

cost.display: $5–$36 per group class; $10–$94 per week self-paced; new 2026 membership tiers $60–$600/month for 1–10 group classes/week

programs.deadline: Rolling — most summer camps run weeks of June 15 – August 22, 2026
programs.description: Marketplace for live, small-group (typically up to 12 students) and 1:1 Zoom-based summer camps and mini-camps for ages 3–18. Topics span Minecraft math, Lego clubs, creative writing, coding, art, science, world languages, and test prep. Strong K–8 catalog with weekly themed camps as short as 5 days. Outschool moved to a credit-based membership model in 2026 alongside its long-running pay-per-class option, so families with multiple kids or weekly camp use can lock in lower per-class rates by subscribing.
programs.scholarshipAid: Outschool Cares scholarship program (need-based, application required); per-class providers occasionally offer their own scholarships; ESA / state-funded education savings accounts accepted in participating states (AZ, etc.)

programs.name: Beast Academy Online (AoPS Elementary Math)

cost.display: $99.99/year per student (covers grades 1–5); $16/month month-to-month; sibling Yearly $64.99/year (requires active Bundle); Bundle (printed books for one level + 1-yr subscription) ~$160; 10% group discount for 5+ subscriptions

programs.deadline: Year-round enrollment — runs continuously; ideal as a summer enrichment supplement or full-year curriculum
programs.description: Self-paced advanced elementary math curriculum from Art of Problem Solving, covering grades 1–5 with the same problem-solving DNA that powers AoPS's MathCounts/AMC pipeline. One subscription gives a single learner access to all five grade levels — kids working ahead are not paywalled by their official grade. Includes adaptive practice, video instruction, and game-style 'Beast Island' progression. AoPS positions Beast Academy as the on-ramp to its 6+ grade Online School and Beast Live Online classes.
programs.scholarshipAid: ClassWallet ESA participating states; some homeschool co-ops bundle at group discount; no formal need-based scholarship listed at the curriculum level
programs.howToStart: Sign up at beastacademy.com/online/enroll, pick monthly or yearly, optionally add the printed books bundle. Free trial of select chapters available.

programs.name: Curious Cardinals 1:1 Mentorship

cost.display: Sessions start at $95/hour; lower rate on 4-month plan, then monthly, highest on pay-as-you-go. Two-month minimum commitment. Money-back guarantee within first 2 weeks.

location.city: Online (Curious Cardinals HQ: San Francisco, CA)

programs.deadline: Rolling; new mentor matches typically within 1–2 weeks of intake
programs.description: Personalized 1:1 mentorship that pairs K–12 students with college and grad-student mentors from top universities for academic tutoring, executive function coaching, and passion-project mentorship. For 4th grade and under (and learners with learning differences), 30-minute sessions are recommended initially. Two main tracks: Academic Mentorship (subject mastery + study skills) and Passion Project Mentorship (a multi-month deliverable a younger student can show off, e.g., a kid-run podcast or a coded game).
programs.scholarshipAid: Limited need-based mentor matching available on request; contact admissions team. No public scholarship page.
programs.howToStart: Submit intake form on curiouscardinals.com, complete a free consultation call, get matched with 1–2 mentor candidates within ~1 week.

programs.name: Synthesis Tutor (AI Math)

cost.display: $20/month or $99/year (Tutor solo plan, ages 5–11, one student); $240/year ($8.25/mo equiv) plan supports up to 7 student profiles per parent account; Synthesis Teams (live group classes, ages 8–14) is $95/month. 7-day free trial.

programs.deadline: Year-round; enroll any time
programs.description: AI-powered K–5 math tutor (ages 5–11) that uses voice + spatial reasoning to teach the full elementary curriculum aligned with US standards: counting, addition/subtraction, multiplication/division, fractions, algebraic thinking. Co-founded by ex-SpaceX/Ad Astra educators. Synthesis also operates Synthesis Teams, a separate live online group experience for ages 8–14 focused on collaborative problem-solving. Particularly strong as a daily 20–30 min summer review or stretch supplement.
programs.scholarshipAid: No formal need-based scholarship publicly listed; gift-of-Synthesis program lets sponsors donate plans; 7-day free trial
programs.howToStart: Start free trial at synthesis.com/tutor, install the iPad/iPhone app, select student grade level. For older kids interested in live classes see synthesis.com/teams.

programs.name: Brain Chase Summer Treasure Hunt

cost.display: Early registration $199 per student for the 5-week program; later/standard registration typically rises ~$50. Family discounts for siblings.

programs.deadline: Program starts June 15, 2026 — register before to secure early-bird $199 pricing
programs.description: 5-week gamified online summer learning program for kids ages 6–16 (designed for grades 2–8). Choose-your-own electives let advanced kids stretch and reluctant learners pick passion-aligned tracks. Self-paced, anywhere, anytime.
programs.scholarshipAid: Limited scholarship spots available on request; family/sibling discounts; school group rates
programs.howToStart: Register for Summer 2026 at brainchase.com/summer-2026-brain-chase-registration/, set up the student dashboard, watch the kickoff video on June 15.

programs.name: Northwestern CTD Academic Day Camps & Enrichment
programs.provider: Northwestern University Center for Talent Development (CTD)

cost.display: Tuition starts at $395 per 1-week half-day course; longer 3-week residential and full-day camps cost more. Need-based financial aid available; CTD partners with the Jack Kent Cooke Foundation.

programs.deadline: Summer 2026 sessions run June 29 – August 7, 2026; registration opens early winter, popular sessions fill before spring
programs.description: Northwestern University's gifted education arm runs week-long, half-day and all-day academic enrichment courses for advanced learners PreK–grade 8 across two eligibility tiers: Amber (open enrollment for PreK–grade 2) and Emerald (testing/portfolio-based eligibility for grades 3–8). Topics span advanced math, science, writing, history, debate, robotics, and creative arts at a faster, deeper pace than typical school. CTD has been operating since 1982 and is one of the four major US gifted summer ecosystems alongside JHU CTY, Duke TIP-successors, and Davidson.
programs.scholarshipAid: Need-based financial aid for most CTD programs; Jack Kent Cooke Foundation partnership for low-income high-ability students; multiple scholarship options listed on the financial aid page
programs.howToStart: For PreK–grade 2 (Amber): apply directly online — open enrollment. For grades 3–8 (Emerald): submit eligibility documentation (test scores or portfolio) with the program application. Forms at ctd.northwestern.edu/eligibility.
