programs.deadline: Rolling — virtual camps launched continually; subscriptions renewable monthly
programs.description: Online coding platform for kids ages 8–16. Three formats: (1) self-paced course library with 24/7 help desk for $29/month, (2) week-long Virtual Camps for $299 covering AI, Python, game development, and Roblox/Minecraft modding, (3) 1:1 private tutoring from instructors at top US universities at $249/month for four 50-minute sessions. Younger campers (8–11) start with block-based platforms like Scratch; older kids (12–16) move to Python and JavaScript. Strong fit for K-8 students who want guided online coding without the in-person commute.
programs.duration: Self-paced; week-long virtual camps; monthly tutoring
programs.dates: Year-round; summer cohorts highlighted
programs.scholarshipAid: Not centrally advertised; 14-day free trial on self-paced courses; complimentary first session for private tutoring
programs.howToStart: Start with the free trial on a self-paced course to gauge interest, then upgrade to a Virtual Camp week or 1:1 tutoring as needed.

programs.name: Tynker — K-12 Self-Paced Coding Platform

cost.display: $54 quarterly or $180/year (or ~$15/month yearly); each plan covers up to 3 children; 30-day money-back guarantee

programs.description: Tynker is the #1 K-12 creative coding platform — used by 1 in 3 U.S. K-8 schools, 150,000 schools globally, and 100M+ kids worldwide. Self-paced gamified courses for ages 5-18 covering block coding (Tynker Jr for pre-readers age 5-7), Minecraft modding, Python, JavaScript, web design, and AI/data science. Quarterly ($54), Yearly ($180), and Lifetime plans all include up to 3 children per family. 30-day money-back guarantee. Full access to Tynker self-paced web platform plus all Tynker iPad apps (Tynker Jr, Tynker, Mod Creator). Strong fit for K-8 students who want to learn at their own pace year-round, especially good for siblings sharing a plan.
programs.scholarshipAid: No formal scholarship program publicly listed; 30-day money-back guarantee on all plans serves as a low-risk trial
programs.howToStart: Start a Free Tynker account at tynker.com/parents — explore Hour of Code activities and free starter games before subscribing. Try the Quarterly plan ($54) first if uncertain; both Quarterly and Yearly include the full self-paced library.

programs.name: Connected Camps — Online Minecraft & Roblox Clubs

cost.display: Sold per session/week via Outschool; typical pricing varies — Free Kid Club Minecraft Server is separate and 100% free

programs.description: Online learning programs run year-round for tech-savvy kids ages 8-13: Minecraft Builder's Club (design + build), Minecraft Survival Club, Girls' Builder's Club, Girls' Survival Club, Roblox Gaming Club, Overwatch Club (ages 9-14), and Smash Ultimate Club. Clubs meet weekly for 90 minutes via expert coach moderation, on Outschool's platform. Compatible with PC, Mac, tablets, phones, Chromebooks, Switch, Xbox, and PS4/PS5. Co-founded by Connie Yowell and U.C. Irvine professor Mimi Ito; designed to convert 'screen time' into structured learning of problem-solving, teamwork, and design. NOTE: pricing is per Outschool listing and varies by club — consult outschool.com Connected Camps storefront. Connected Camps also runs a separate FREE Kid Club Minecraft Server (moderated public sandbox) for kids without subscriptions.
programs.scholarshipAid: Outschool Cares scholarship program may apply (Connected Camps lists on Outschool); state Education Savings Account funds (AZ/FL/AR) usable through Outschool
programs.howToStart: Browse Connected Camps storefront on Outschool to see live pricing and current cohort availability, OR join the FREE Kid Club Minecraft Server first to test fit before subscribing.

programs.name: Khan Academy Kids — Free Early Learning App (Ages 2-8)

cost.display: 100% free — no ads, no subscriptions, no in-app purchases

programs.description: Free educational app for children ages 2-8 (PreK through grade 2). 5,000+ activities and books across reading/phonics, math, social-emotional learning, and creative play. Built in partnership with Stanford Graduate School of Education. Aligned with Head Start standards and Common Core. COPPA-compliant. Featured five-character cast (Kodi, Reya, Peck, Sandy, Ollo) guides kids through structured learning paths. Available iOS, Android, Amazon Fire (beta on Android/Amazon). Multiple awards including Common Sense Media Top Rated Educational App, Children's Technology Review Editor's Choice, Parents' Choice Gold. Strongest fit for K-2 home reinforcement, summer learning loss prevention, and pre-K readiness. Khan Academy proper (separate program, already in DB) covers grades 3+.
programs.scholarshipAid: 100% free — no scholarship needed; no paid tier exists
programs.howToStart: Download the Khan Academy Kids app (App Store, Google Play, or Amazon Appstore) — no account required to start, but creating a parent account unlocks per-child progress tracking and a Library mode.

programs.name: NASA Kids' Club & K-8 STEM Resources
programs.description: NASA's official free K-8 STEM portal. Hands-on activities, games, videos, and stories — kids can launch rockets, build a Moon Habitat, explore the Solar System, and solve space-themed puzzles. Content organized by grade band (K-4, 5-8, 9-12) with separate hub pages per band. Includes the NASA EXPRESS newsletter (workshops, contests, student challenges, science experiments), STEM Multimedia library, and 'NASA at Home' family activity packets. Spanish-language sub-portal (Sistema Solar) available. Strong fit for elementary/middle school enrichment, especially for science fair prep, summer STEM exposure, and supplementing classroom curriculum. Not a structured 'camp' but a curated portal to thousands of NASA-published activities, lesson plans, and challenges — many designed for self-led or parent-guided use at home.
programs.scholarshipAid: 100% free — no application required
programs.howToStart: Visit nasa.gov/learning-resources/nasa-kids-club/ — no signup required. Subscribe to the NASA EXPRESS newsletter (free) for weekly student-challenges, contests, and seasonal hands-on activities targeted to your child's grade band.

programs.name: CodeCombat — Game-Based Coding (Python & JavaScript)

cost.display: First chapter free; home premium reportedly $10-$40/month range; school pricing by quote

programs.description: Game-based coding platform recommended for grades 4-12 (ages 9+) where students learn real Python and JavaScript by playing through fantasy game levels. Includes the original CodeCombat (action RPG style) and Ozaria (immersive narrative game aligned to middle-school CSTA + ISTE standards). First chapter is free for any student. Home premium subscription typically $10-$40/month range (verify current price on site). School/classroom pricing is by quote. Clever and Google Classroom integrations supported. Ozaria works on Windows PCs, Chromebooks, and Macs in a modern browser. Strongest fit for 4th-8th graders ready to graduate from block-based coding (Scratch/Tynker Jr) into typed-language programming.
programs.scholarshipAid: Not publicly advertised; first chapter free serves as no-risk trial
programs.howToStart: Create a free CodeCombat account at codecombat.com — kids can play through Chapter 1 (Kithgard Dungeon) at zero cost. Decide on premium based on engagement level after the free chapter; classroom teachers can also sign students up for Ozaria's free first unit.

programs.name: Russian School of Mathematics (RSM) Online — Summer & Year-Round

cost.display: Reported range $41-$110 per lesson depending on grade and program; exact tuition only via tuition-request form

programs.description: Online after-school math enrichment grades 2-10 (year-round school year program; physical-location program covers K-12 across 60+ U.S. branches). 2026 summer schedule June 29 - August 6 with 6-week and 3-week tracks: math reinforcement, math competition prep (AMC 8 / Math Kangaroo / Math Olympiad), and special enrichment courses including Coding (JavaScript for middle school), Summer Chess (grades 1-5), STEAM (K-1), and Math/Science/Art Lab (K-1). Twice-weekly classes (1.5-2 hrs in-person grades 1-3; 2 hrs online grades 4-10). Curriculum is a continuous K-12 vertically-aligned program emphasizing depth + abstract reasoning, modeled on Russian/Eastern European mathematics pedagogy. Placement test required for entry; tuition only available by submitting the tuition-request form. Strong fit for ambitious K-8 math students or families wanting summer-loss prevention beyond a worksheet program.
programs.scholarshipAid: Not publicly advertised on landing pages; some local branches offer financial aid — call the local branch director directly to ask
programs.howToStart: Submit the tuition-request form on mathschool.com to get the PDF with grade-specific pricing for your region/track. Schedule a placement test (free) — RSM uses results to assign the right level rather than relying on grade alone, so a strong 5th grader may place into the 6th-grade curriculum.

programs.name: Camp Invention 2026 — Spark

cost.display: ~$245-295/wk (use code CIFUN25 by 3/31 or CIFUN20 by 4/28 for $20-25 off; sibling discounts SIBNAT30 = $60 off / SIBNAT40 = $120+ off)

programs.description: Camp Invention 2026 'Spark' theme runs at 1500+ host elementary schools nationwide. Four hands-on STEM modules: Make Waves (entrepreneurship), Space Morphers (planet ecosystems + DIY rockets), The Infringers (cryptography + IP), and Spark Innovation Lab. Led by qualified local educators; rising K-6.

programs.name: 4-H Summer Camp (state Cooperative Extension network)

cost.display: $145-$300/wk typical, sliding scale + scholarship aid widely available

programs.deadline: Varies by state; most open Jan-Feb
programs.description: 4-H operates summer day + residential camps in every US state through the Cooperative Extension at land-grant universities. Activities span outdoor skills, agriculture, STEM, robotics, equine programs, aquatics, ropes courses, and animal science. Camp lengths from 3 days (day camps) to 6-day sleepaway. Strong scholarship pipeline. Find your state via 4-h.org/parents/find-your-4-h.

programs.name: FIRST LEGO League Explore (FLL Explore)
programs.provider: FIRST (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology)

cost.display: Team registration ~$110-160 + LEGO kit costs; many schools/libraries host free teams

programs.deadline: Season starts August; teams form May-July
programs.description: FIRST LEGO League Explore is the K-4 introduction to FIRST's robotics ecosystem. Small teams (2-6 kids) build motorized LEGO models around an annual challenge theme, present to judges at season-end Festival. Builds engineering thinking + presentation skills. Most teams formed through schools, libraries, or community groups. Older sibling track FLL Challenge (grades 4-8) is the natural progression.

programs.name: FIRST LEGO League Challenge

cost.display: Team registration ~$225-275 + EV3/SPIKE Prime kit; school-team subsidies common

programs.deadline: Season opens August; team registration through district/regional
programs.description: FLL Challenge is the grade 4-8 robotics + research competition. Teams of up to 10 build autonomous LEGO robots, conduct research project on annual theme, compete at qualifying tournaments through state championships. Combines engineering, programming, research, presentation, and teamwork. The most accessible serious-robotics on-ramp before high-school FIRST Tech Challenge.

programs.name: Junior Achievement (JA) BizTown + JA Finance Park

cost.display: Free for participating school-district kids (corporate sponsorship)

programs.deadline: School-arranged field trips throughout school year + summer programs at some affiliates
programs.description: JA BizTown (grades 4-6) is a 1-day immersive simulation where students run a mini-economy as workers, consumers, and citizens in a mock town. JA Finance Park (grades 7-8) is the personal finance + budgeting equivalent. Both delivered through 100+ JA local affiliates. Most schools coordinate field trips; some affiliates run summer day camps. Teaches financial literacy, entrepreneurship, and economic citizenship.

programs.name: National Park Service Junior Ranger Program

cost.display: Free at all 400+ NPS sites (some park entrance fees may apply)

programs.deadline: None; year-round at any park
programs.description: Visit any NPS site, pick up a Junior Ranger booklet at the visitor center, complete age-appropriate activities (hike a trail, attend a ranger talk, draw something you saw), get sworn in as a Junior Ranger and earn a badge. Free. Available at all 400+ NPS sites including national parks, monuments, historic sites, recreation areas. Online versions exist for sites you can't visit. Kids who collect badges across many parks build a portfolio of outdoor + civic engagement.

programs.name: iD Tech Online Camps

cost.display: Online camps ~$499-799/wk; financial aid available; in-person at 50+ universities ~$1500-3000/wk

programs.deadline: Rolling weekly sessions June-August; book by April for popular tracks
programs.description: iD Tech Online runs small-group (max 5:1 ratio) live-instructor coding camps for ages 7-19. Tracks include Roblox, Minecraft modding, Python, JavaScript, Unity game dev, AI, machine learning, and YouTube content. Each session ~$499-799/week of half-day or full-day virtual sessions. In-person sister camps at Stanford, MIT, NYU, Caltech, UCLA, Princeton, and 50+ partner universities. Financial aid via Campers' Choice scholarships.

programs.name: Outschool — small-group online classes

cost.display: Per-class pricing ~$10-30/session; many free trials; financial aid via the Outschool Foundation

programs.deadline: None; classes start weekly
programs.description: Marketplace of 100,000+ small-group online classes from independent expert teachers. Subjects span Dungeons & Dragons clubs, creative writing workshops, Python coding, advanced math, language conversation circles, art studios, and one-off topical seminars (the science of pizza, the history of skateboarding, etc.). Excellent for kids with niche interests not served by local options. Per-class pricing ~$10-30/session; many free intro classes. Outschool Foundation provides need-based aid.

programs.name: Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) + Beast Academy

cost.display: Beast Academy Online ~$15/mo subscription; AoPS courses ~$300-600/term; AoPS Academy ~$400-700/wk for in-person camps

programs.deadline: Rolling enrollment for online; summer intensives book by April
programs.description: Beast Academy is the K-5 problem-solving math curriculum (online subscription or print books with workbooks). AoPS Online is the grade 5+ enrichment platform with structured courses, MATHCOUNTS prep, and AMC competition prep. AoPS Academy operates in-person locations in 15+ US metros (incl. Bellevue WA) for after-school + summer intensives. Strongest path for the kid who finds school math too easy and needs depth, not acceleration. Pipeline to Math Olympiad and high-school MOP.

programs.name: Khan Academy + Khan Academy Kids (free)
programs.deadline: None; year-round self-paced
programs.description: Khan Academy Kids is the free K-2 app (iOS, Android, web) covering reading, math, social-emotional learning. Khan Academy proper covers grade 3+ math, science, history, computing, economics, and AP test prep — entirely free. Ad-free, no subscription. Pairs well with district summer 'don't lose progress' assignments. Khan teacher tools allow parents to assign + track progress. Quietly the highest-leverage free K-12 academic resource on the internet.

programs.name: Smithsonian Learning Lab + Smithsonian Summer Camps

cost.display: Online resources free; summer camps at affiliate museums vary $200-500/wk; financial aid available

programs.deadline: Affiliate camp registration opens Jan-March
programs.description: Smithsonian Learning Lab provides free online K-12 curriculum + 1M+ digital resources from 21 Smithsonian museums. Beyond DC, the Smithsonian Affiliate Museums network has 200+ partner museums across all 50 states (e.g., Pacific Science Center is a Smithsonian Affiliate). Many run summer camps for K-8 with Smithsonian-developed curriculum. Find your nearest at affiliations.si.edu/affiliate-list.

programs.name: Code.org Hour of Code + Code.org After School
programs.deadline: Hour of Code week early December; year-round content
programs.description: Code.org runs the Hour of Code (Dec event reaching 100M+ kids globally) plus year-round CS curriculum used in 45% of US schools. Self-paced courses progress from drag-block (CS Fundamentals A-F for grades K-5) through real Python (CS Discoveries grades 6-8). All free. Schools can adopt the full curriculum. Parents can use the courses solo with their kid. Major bridge for kids interested in coding before paying for iD Tech.

programs.name: NASA STEM Engagement Virtual Events (Glenn + Marshall + IV&V)

cost.display: 100% free; subscribe to NASA EXPRESS newsletter for current event listings

programs.deadline: Event-specific; registrations open ~2 months before event date
programs.description: Multiple NASA centers (Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, IV&V Facility in West Virginia) run free virtual STEM events for K-12 students. Each is typically 1-2 hours: presentation by NASA scientist/engineer + Q&A. Topics rotate (Mars exploration, ISS science, materials engineering, etc.). Parent registration required for younger kids. Subscribe to the NASA EXPRESS newsletter for new event announcements. Best K-8 STEM credential you can get without leaving your living room.

programs.name: Mad Science Summer Camps

cost.display: Varies by franchise — typical week-long camps ~$200–$400 (half-day) or $350–$600 (full-day)

programs.description: Mad Science is a science enrichment franchise (operating since 1985) running themed weekly summer day camps for kids ages 4–12. Themes rotate weekly: Secret Agent Lab, Robot Academy, Digging Dinos, NASA Camp, Science of Slime, Inventors Camp, and more. Camps are typically half- or full-day at host sites (community centers, schools, parks-and-rec, hosting partners), with branded experiments and take-home science kits. 100+ franchise territories operate across the US and Canada — coverage varies by metro.
programs.dates: June–August 2026 (varies by franchise; registration typically opens Feb–Mar)
programs.scholarshipAid: Varies by franchise — some host-site partnerships (parks-and-rec) offer subsidized pricing; ask the local franchise about sliding scale
programs.howToStart: Use the franchise locator at madscience.org/find-a-location, then register through the local franchise site or host-partner portal.

programs.name: Engineering For Kids Summer Camps

cost.display: Varies by franchise — typical week-long camps ~$250–$450 (half-day) or $400–$700 (full-day)

programs.description: Engineering For Kids is a STEM-focused enrichment franchise running hands-on engineering camps for ages 4–14. Camp categories include Aerospace, Chemical, Civil, Electrical, Environmental, Forensics, Industrial, Marine, Mechanical, and Mechatronics engineering, plus robotics and coding. Camps are typically half- or full-day weekly sessions at school, community-center, or franchise locations. 2026 nationwide registration opened March 1, 2026 — locations sell out quickly in popular metros.
programs.dates: June–August 2026 (national registration opened Mar 1, 2026)
programs.scholarshipAid: Varies by franchise — some locations partner with host parks-and-rec for subsidized pricing; no central scholarship fund
programs.howToStart: Locate your closest EFK at engineeringforkids.com/find-a-location, then register through the local franchise booking page.

programs.name: Play-Well TEKnologies LEGO® Engineering Summer Camps

cost.display: Varies by host site — typical week-long camps ~$250–$425 (half-day, M–F)

programs.description: Play-Well TEKnologies (founded 1997) runs LEGO®-based engineering summer camps for ages 5–14, with curriculum designed by engineers. Themed weekly camps include Pokémon Engineering, Dinosaur Engineering, Minecraft, Star Wars Engineering, and general engineering & robotics. Camps run as half-day or full-day weekly sessions hosted at parks-and-rec, libraries, schools, museums, and community centers across 40+ states. Registration is typically through the host site, not Play-Well directly.
programs.dates: June–August 2026 (varies by host site; many open Feb–Mar)
programs.scholarshipAid: Varies by host site — some parks-and-rec partners offer income-based subsidies; ask host directly
programs.howToStart: Search by zip at schedule.play-well.org to find a camp near you; register through the host (not Play-Well) for those camps.

programs.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of America (local club)

cost.display: $20-30/year typical membership at most clubs; many clubs FREE for low-income; sliding-scale + scholarship for activities

programs.deadline: Year-round enrollment
programs.description: BGCA operates 4,500+ local Clubs serving 4M+ kids annually. Annual membership is $20-30 in most clubs and grants access to after-school, summer, weekend programs covering academics, arts, sports, leadership, STEM, and college prep. Many clubs operate as virtual childcare for working parents. The 'Triple Play' health program, 'Money Matters' financial literacy, and 'Be Great' college prep are nationally consistent.

programs.name: YMCA Youth Programs (local Y umbrella)

cost.display: Annual membership ~$300-700/family with sliding scale (Open Doors); many programs free for members; non-member day camps $150-300/wk

programs.deadline: Year-round; summer camp registration opens Jan-Feb
programs.description: Y-USA umbrella covers 2,700+ local YMCA branches across the US. Programs include after-school (Y-CAP), day camps, residential camps (e.g., Camp Orkila, Camp Cheerio), youth sports leagues, swim lessons, and Achievers leadership pipeline. The Open Doors financial assistance program covers 100% of membership for qualifying families.

programs.name: Scholastic Summer Reading Challenge
programs.deadline: Annual program runs May-September
programs.description: Free annual summer reading program from Scholastic. Kids log reading minutes, unlock weekly streaks + earn rewards. Curated book lists by grade level. Teacher dashboards available; parent-led use also fully supported. Pairs naturally with public library summer reading clubs. The 'Read-A-Palooza' track adds challenges for advanced readers grades 4-6.

programs.name: Google CS First
programs.deadline: None; year-round self-paced
programs.description: Free Google-developed coding curriculum for grades 4-8 using Scratch. 8 themed clubs (Storytelling, Game Design, Music & Sound, Animation, Friends, Sports, Fashion & Design, Art) with 8 hour-long sessions each. Designed for clubs, classrooms, or self-led learning. No CS background required. Pairs well with Code.org Fundamentals as the next step up.

programs.name: Microsoft DigiGirlz Day

location.city: Microsoft offices in 30+ US locations + virtual

programs.deadline: Events year-round; register 2-4 weeks before
programs.description: Free 1-day events at Microsoft offices specifically for middle school girls (and gender-expansive youth) interested in tech. Includes hands-on coding/AI/cybersecurity workshops, panels with women technologists, and tour of Microsoft campus. Most Microsoft offices host 2-4 events per year. Excellent peer-network building. Confidence: high registration windows are short — popular Seattle/Redmond events fill in days.

programs.name: Carnegie Hall Link Up

cost.display: 100% free curriculum + concert participation; school partner only

programs.deadline: School-year program; partner orchestras enroll schools spring/summer
programs.description: Free K-3 music education program partnering with 90+ symphony orchestras across the US (e.g., Seattle Symphony, San Francisco Symphony, LA Phil, NY Phil). Full curriculum + culminating concert where students perform alongside the orchestra. Schools must enroll, but the program is free. Find your local partner orchestra at carnegiehall.org/link-up.

programs.name: PJ Library — Free Jewish Children's Books
programs.deadline: Year-round signup
programs.description: Free monthly Jewish-themed children's books mailed to participating families with kids ages 0-11. Funded by the Harold Grinspoon Foundation. No religious affiliation required. Books span picture books through middle-grade chapter books. Companion 'PJ Our Way' track for ages 9-12 lets kids choose their own books. Excellent literacy + cultural enrichment combo for any family interested in Jewish stories/values.

programs.name: National Geographic Kids — free resources + Slingshot Challenge

cost.display: 100% free online; Slingshot Challenge open to ages 13-18

programs.deadline: Slingshot Challenge submission ~mid-March annually
programs.description: Free Nat Geo Kids content covering science, geography, animals, and exploration: games, videos, articles, and Almanac series. The Slingshot Challenge invites kids 13-18 to submit 1-minute videos about climate-action ideas (winners get $10K and Nat Geo mentorship). Younger kids access curated explorer-led content + free educator resources. Great anchor for science-curious K-8 kids.

programs.name: PBS Kids — summer learning + at-home activities
programs.deadline: None
programs.description: Free educational PBS Kids programming (Daniel Tiger, Wild Kratts, Curious George, Molly of Denali, Xavier Riddle, etc.) plus at-home activity guides keyed to the shows. Summer learning curriculum from PBS LearningMedia for educators + parents. PBS Kids GO! older-track app for grades 1-3. Quietly the highest-leverage free preschool + early-elementary content available, ad-free.

programs.name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program (CAP)

cost.display: Annual dues ~$45-55 + uniform; financial assistance available; encampment fees subsidized

programs.deadline: Year-round enrollment
programs.description: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program is the auxiliary of the US Air Force open to ages 12-18. Cadets earn promotions through aerospace education, leadership, physical fitness, and character development modules. Free orientation rides in CAP aircraft. National encampments + activities (cybersecurity, drone, STEM tracks) heavily subsidized. Pipeline to USAF Academy + ROTC. 1,500+ local squadrons nationwide. Excellent leadership credential for kids interested in aviation/military pathways.

programs.name: Junior Master Gardener Program
programs.provider: International Junior Master Gardener (USDA Coop Extension)

cost.display: Curriculum guides ~$25-40; Coop Extension-led groups often free

programs.deadline: Rolling enrollment
programs.description: Free curriculum-based youth gardening program partnered with USDA Cooperative Extension. Levels 1 (3rd-5th grade) and 2 (6th-8th grade) cover plant growth, ecology, food/fiber, soils, water, environmental horticulture. Kids earn certifications + lead service projects. Implemented through schools, after-school clubs, scouts, 4-H, or families. Excellent for the kid who likes nature + hands-on but isn't into structured camps.

programs.name: Destination Imagination (DI)

cost.display: Team registration ~$200-300 + materials; school-team subsidies common

location.city: Nationwide tournaments via 38 state Affiliates + 30 countries

programs.deadline: Tournament registration Sep-Jan; finals March-May
programs.description: Team-based creative problem-solving competition. Teams of 2-7 kids tackle a 'Team Challenge' (technical/scientific/structural/improv/service-learning) over months — building solutions from scratch. State-level tournaments feed into Global Finals. K-2 division is non-competitive. Builds collaboration, project management, hands-on engineering, and presentation skills. Compares well with FLL but emphasizes creativity + theatrical presentation more than pure robotics.

programs.name: National History Day (NHD)

cost.display: Free for student participation in most district/state contests

programs.deadline: District contests Feb-March; state April-May; nationals June
programs.description: Annual academic competition where students conduct original historical research on a chosen topic and present via paper, exhibit, performance, documentary, or website. Junior division (grades 6-8) and Senior division (9-12). District → state → national progression. Builds research, writing, critical analysis, and presentation skills. Nationals at U Maryland in June. Excellent humanities-track credential — comparable in middle school to FLL for STEM.

programs.name: CISV International — Village + Interchange + Step Up

cost.display: Village ~$2,500-3,500 + airfare; financial aid via national chapters; Interchange ~$1,500

programs.deadline: Applications due Oct-Dec for following summer
programs.description: CISV International runs structured peace-education programs across 60+ countries since 1951. The Village (ages 11) is a 4-week residential program with kids from 12 countries learning collaboration through games + cultural activities. Interchange (ages 12-15) pairs delegations of 4-6 kids for reciprocal home stays. Step Up (ages 14-15) is a 3-week leadership-focused program. US national chapters (cisvusa.org) coordinate selection + delegation training. Strong financial aid pipeline. One of the most respected international peace-education programs for tweens.

programs.name: Concordia Language Villages

location.city: Bemidji + multiple sites in Minnesota northwoods

programs.deadline: Sessions June-August; popular weeks book by April
programs.description: Language immersion summer camps in 14+ languages (Spanish, French, German, Mandarin, Japanese, Russian, Arabic, Korean, Italian, Portuguese, Swedish, Norwegian, Finnish, Danish + occasional ASL/Hindi). Located on dedicated themed villages in Northern Minnesota. Kids live the language: signs, songs, meals, activities all in target language. Sessions 1, 2, or 4 weeks. The 4-week sessions can earn high school language credit. Need-based scholarships called 'Villager Aid' cover up to 100%.

programs.name: EF Language Travel Camps

cost.display: $3,500-7,000 for 2-3 weeks abroad incl. lodging; airfare extra; some scholarship via EF Educational Tours

location.city: London, Paris, Madrid, Barcelona, Munich, Tokyo + 50 cities

programs.deadline: Sessions June-August; book by March for popular destinations
programs.description: EF runs language immersion summer camps in 50+ cities across Europe + Asia. Younger track (10-13) has structured group programs with chaperones; older track (14+) has more independence. Programs are 2-3 weeks: morning language classes + afternoon excursions + weekend cultural activities. Older sibling of EF's high-school NSLI-Y-style trips. Generally cheaper alternative to NSLI-Y (which is free but very selective). Reasonable middle-school international option.
_unverifiedFields: specific 2026 K-8 minimum age (varies by destination)

programs.name: WWOOF (World-Wide Opportunities on Organic Farms) Family Stays

cost.display: WWOOF host-country membership ~$30-60/yr; food + lodging FREE in exchange for help on farm; family pays only travel

programs.deadline: Year-round; arrange directly with hosts 1-3 months ahead
programs.description: Volunteer-on-organic-farms exchange. Family pays for membership in destination country's WWOOF chapter (~$30-60/yr) + travel; in return, host provides food + lodging in exchange for ~4-6 hours/day farm work (weeding, animal care, harvesting, building, etc.). 12,000+ host farms in 130+ countries. Many hosts welcome families with kids — often the kid-friendly hosts are flagged. Powerful immersive cultural + agricultural exposure. Best ages 8+ (kids who can contribute meaningfully). Not all host countries accept kids — verify country-by-country.

programs.name: MATHCOUNTS (middle school math competition)

cost.display: FREE for participating school teams; individual track also free

programs.deadline: Coaching September-January; chapter competitions February; nationals May
programs.description: The premier US middle school math competition since 1983. Teams of 4 from each school + individual students compete in chapter → state → national competition. Problems range from algebra/geometry/number theory/combinatorics. National finals at Walt Disney World every May. School registration is FREE (sponsored by Raytheon, Northrop Grumman, US DoD STEM, NSPE). Strong AoPS + Beast Academy integration for prep. Pipeline to AMC + Math Olympiad + RSI in HS.

programs.name: VEX IQ Challenge (elementary + middle school robotics)

cost.display: VEX IQ kit ~$300-500 + team registration ~$100; school-team grants common via REC Foundation

programs.deadline: Season starts April; tournaments fall through spring; world championships May
programs.description: VEX IQ is the elementary + middle school division of VEX Robotics — kid-friendly snap-together robotics platform vs FIRST's LEGO Mindstorms. Annual game-based challenge; teams design + program robots to compete in skills + alliance matches. World championships May at Disney. Compares well with FIRST LEGO League — VEX is more focused on game strategy, FLL more on research-project + robot. Some kids do both. REC Foundation grants for new teams.

programs.name: eCYBERMISSION (US Army STEM competition)

cost.display: FREE; team prizes up to $9,000 in US Savings Bonds

programs.deadline: Registration opens August; project submission late February; finals June
programs.description: Free Army-sponsored STEM competition for grades 6-9. Teams of 3-4 students + a 'team advisor' (teacher or parent) tackle a community problem using STEM research. Each team submits a Mission Folder describing their work. State + regional + national winners. Top national prizes are $9,000 in savings bonds per team member. Strong second-tier alternative to MATHCOUNTS for kids more interested in applied research than competition math.

programs.name: Future City Competition (DiscoverE)

cost.display: Free participation; school + non-profit teams welcome

programs.deadline: Project work fall; regional competitions Jan-Feb; finals Feb in DC
programs.description: Annual engineering competition for grades 6-8. Teams design a 'future city' addressing an annual real-world challenge (recent themes: thriving with climate change, future of waste, etc.). Submit a virtual city in SimCity, a 1500-word essay, a 25-square-foot scale model, and a 7-min presentation. Regional winners advance to national finals in DC each February. Free to enter. Strong fit for kids who like systems thinking + creative engineering across multiple disciplines.

programs.name: Science Olympiad Division B (middle school)
programs.deadline: Season starts September; regionals Feb-March; nationals May
programs.description: Team-based science competition for grades 6-9 (Division B). Teams of 15 compete in 23 events spanning biology, chemistry, physics, earth science, engineering, and 'study events' (Anatomy, Disease Detectives, etc.) + 'build events' (Air Trajectory, Bridge Building, etc.). Regional → state → national progression. Schools register teams. Strong combination of academic depth + engineering hands-on. Prep starts September; February is when the season heats up.

programs.name: American Museum of Natural History Discovery Squad + Children's Camps

cost.display: 1-week day camps ~$575-650; member discount 10%; needs-based aid via AMNH Education

programs.deadline: Member registration February; general March-April
programs.description: AMNH runs week-long age-banded summer camps using the museum's collections + Hayden Planetarium + Discovery Room. Themes vary: paleontology, astrophysics, marine biology, natural history. Kids work with AMNH educators + sometimes scientists. Member registration opens 3 weeks before general — membership pays back via earlier access. East-coast equivalent of Pacific Science Center / Burke Museum camps.

programs.name: Exploratorium Summer Camps
programs.deadline: Member registration February; general March-April
programs.description: Exploratorium is one of the most influential science museums globally — pioneered the 'hands-on' museum model. Summer camps for ages 8-14 are tinkering- + maker-focused: kids build, take apart, hack, prototype using the museum's exhibits as starting points. Themes rotate (Tinker, Cardboard Engineering, Sound + Music, Light + Color). Bay Area's premier hands-on science camp.

programs.name: Field Museum Summer Camps + Junior Curators

cost.display: 1-week ~$425-575; member discount 10%; scholarship via Field Museum Education

programs.deadline: Member registration January; general February-March
programs.description: Field Museum (Chicago, home of Sue the T-Rex) runs age-banded summer camps for grades K-8. Themes span paleontology, ancient civilizations (Egypt, Maya), animal kingdom, ecosystems. Junior Curators track for older kids includes behind-the-scenes lab visits. Strong Midwest equivalent to AMNH / Smithsonian camps.
_unverifiedFields: specific 2026 dates and pricing — verify on field museum education page

programs.name: Apple Camp at Apple Store (free)

cost.display: 100% free — including iPad use during sessions

programs.deadline: Sessions July-August; sign up via Apple's Today at Apple in late June
programs.description: Free 90-minute Apple Camp sessions held at every Apple Store nationwide each summer. Topics rotate (animation with Keynote, sketch + animate with Procreate, music with GarageBand, video editing). Kids use Apple devices provided in-store; no purchase or device ownership required. Sessions are usually 3-day series (1 session per day). Sign up at apple.com/today/series. Often the easiest free creative-tech intro for elementary kids.

programs.name: Best Buddies International (school + community chapters)
programs.deadline: Year-round; chapters form at start of school year
programs.description: Best Buddies pairs students with intellectual + developmental disabilities (IDD) with peer 'buddies' for one-to-one friendships, structured activities, and community-building. Middle School Buddies (grades 6-8) + High School Buddies (9-12) operate as school clubs. Pairs build authentic friendships across difference. Strong inclusion + leadership signal — recognized by selective colleges. Schools start chapters via bestbuddies.org.

programs.name: Foundation for Jewish Camp — One Happy Camper grant

cost.display: OHC grant: $1,000 for first-time campers; total camp ~$1,500-3,500/wk

location.city: 150+ Jewish overnight camps in US + Canada

programs.deadline: OHC grant applications open Nov-Feb for following summer
programs.description: Foundation for Jewish Camp's One Happy Camper grant gives $1,000 to first-time Jewish overnight campers, no income test required. 150+ partner camps span Reform, Conservative, Orthodox, Reconstructionist, Renewal, secular-Jewish, special-needs (Camp Ramah), and culinary themes. Search by camp at jewishcamp.org/find-a-camp. Need-based aid stacks on top of OHC grant.

programs.name: Catholic Heart Workcamp (CHWC)

cost.display: ~$420-450/wk + travel; financial aid via parish + diocese

programs.deadline: Sessions June-August; book by Feb-March for popular sites
programs.description: Week-long Catholic service mission camps. Teams of teens travel to 60+ host cities (US + a few intl) and serve local communities — home repairs, eldercare, food bank work, ministry. Strong Catholic identity programming (daily Mass, prayer groups) but accepts non-Catholic siblings/friends. 6th graders accepted in some locations (junior camps). Powerful service + spiritual development combo.

programs.name: Hispanic Heritage Foundation — Youth Awards + LOFT

cost.display: FREE for selected applicants; scholarships up to $5,000

programs.deadline: Youth Awards open Sep-Dec; LOFT applications spring
programs.description: HHF Youth Awards: regional + national recognition for Hispanic high schoolers in 8 categories (STEM, business, healthcare, arts, etc.) with $1,000-$5,000 scholarships. LOFT (Latinos On Fast Track) is the year-round leadership pipeline for grades 8-12 with mentorship, college prep, and free national summit attendance. Applications opens fall of each school year. Strong cultural-identity + leadership combo for Latino youth.

programs.name: Plum Village Mindfulness Family Retreats

cost.display: Family donation: ~$300-700/wk per family member; sliding scale; no one turned away for lack of funds

location.city: Plum Village monasteries: France, Vermont (Blue Cliff), New York (Magnolia Grove), California (Deer Park)

programs.deadline: Summer family retreats July-August; book by April
programs.description: Family mindfulness retreats at Plum Village monasteries (France headquarters + 3 US sites). Founded by Thich Nhat Hanh (Vietnamese Buddhist teacher). Kids' programs run parallel to adult retreats with their own age-banded mindfulness, walking meditation, and 'pebble meditation' for younger kids. Vegetarian meals. Strong intergenerational community-building. Sliding-scale fees, no one turned away.

programs.name: Friends General Conference (FGC) Quaker Family Camp

location.city: Annual gathering site rotates (recent: PA, OH, NY, MI)

programs.deadline: Annual Gathering early July; registration spring
programs.description: Annual Quaker Gathering: 5-day intergenerational camp at a college campus. Programs span workshops + worship-sharing + recreation + age-banded children's program (ages 3 through HS). Quaker community-driven, queer-affirming, peace-focused. Sliding-scale 'Equalization Fund' covers up to 100% for low-income families. Kids' program (Junior Gathering for grades K-9) runs parallel to adult workshops.

programs.name: Asian American Journalists Association (AAJA) youth programs

cost.display: FREE for selected; covers travel + lodging for JCamp

programs.deadline: JCamp applications due February for August program
programs.description: AAJA's JCamp is a free 6-day journalism program for ~30 selected high school students from across the US, Canada, and beyond. AAJA covers travel + lodging for accepted students. Focus on multimedia journalism, AAPI representation in media, and career mentorship. Highly selective (~5% acceptance rate). One of the most prestigious journalism programs for AAPI teens. Note: HS focus, but worth knowing for parents planning ahead from 8th grade.

programs.name: Hispanic Scholarship Fund (HSF) Youth Leadership Institute

cost.display: FREE for selected scholars + scholarship pipeline ($500-$5,000)

location.city: Online + regional summits in major US metros

programs.deadline: Spring application; programs run year-round
programs.description: HSF Youth Leadership Institute: pipeline program for Hispanic/Latino youth (grades 7-12) with mentorship, leadership training, college prep workshops, and pathway to HSF scholarships ($500-$5K). Free for selected applicants. Regional summits in NYC, LA, Miami, Houston, Chicago, DC. Online programming year-round. Strong combination of cultural-identity + academic + leadership development.

programs.name: Sierra Club Inspiring Connections Outdoors (ICO)

cost.display: 100% free for participating youth — Sierra Club volunteers fund all gear + transportation

location.city: 50+ ICO chapters in major US cities

programs.deadline: Year-round trips; chapter-coordinated
programs.description: Sierra Club ICO connects under-resourced urban youth with the outdoors via free guided trips: hikes, camping, kayaking, snowshoeing, backpacking. Volunteer-led; gear, transport, and food covered by Sierra Club fundraising. 50+ city chapters (Seattle, Bay Area, Chicago, NYC, Atlanta, Miami, etc.). Most chapters partner with schools, BGCA, YMCA, or community centers to reach kids. Excellent low-barrier outdoor entry for kids whose families don't have outdoor gear/experience.

programs.name: National Wildlife Federation Eco-Schools USA
programs.deadline: Year-round school enrollment
programs.description: NWF Eco-Schools USA is the school-based environmental sustainability program — kids audit their school's environmental footprint (energy, water, waste, biodiversity, schoolyard habitat) and lead improvement projects. 7 'pathways' (climate, energy, water, waste, etc.). Schools earn Bronze / Silver / Green Flag certifications. FREE curriculum + tools. International (Eco-Schools active in 70+ countries). Strong fit for kids interested in environmental leadership at school.

programs.name: NPS Every Kid Outdoors (free 4th grade pass)
programs.provider: National Park Service / White House initiative

cost.display: 100% FREE pass — admits 4th grader + 3 adults + all minor siblings to all NPS sites

programs.deadline: Pass valid Sep 1 - Aug 31 of 4th grade year
programs.description: Every Kid Outdoors pass gives ALL US 4th graders FREE entry to all 400+ NPS sites (national parks, monuments, historic sites, recreation areas) PLUS US Forest Service + US Fish & Wildlife sites + US Army Corps lands. Pass admits the 4th grader + 3 adults + all minor siblings in a single vehicle. Get yours at everykidoutdoors.gov by completing a short activity. Valid Sep 1 - Aug 31 of 4th grade year. Easy way to do an entire family of national parks vacations free.

programs.name: Audubon for Kids — citizen science + Junior Birder

cost.display: FREE for all youth participation (Audubon Adventures curriculum ~$50 for educators)

programs.deadline: Christmas Bird Count Dec 14 - Jan 5; Great Backyard Bird Count Feb; year-round chapter activities
programs.description: National Audubon Society offers free youth bird-focused citizen science: Christmas Bird Count for Kids, Great Backyard Bird Count (Feb, family-friendly), Junior Birder programs at 500+ local Audubon chapters + nature centers. Audubon Adventures is the K-6 in-school curriculum. Combines real science contribution + outdoor time + photography skills. Excellent low-barrier entry to STEM + environment for elementary kids.

programs.name: NOAA Planet Stewards Education Project

cost.display: FREE curriculum + project funding up to $5,000 for educator-led student projects

programs.deadline: Project funding applications due September each year
programs.description: NOAA's Planet Stewards program funds K-12 educator-led student projects on climate, oceans, and weather. Up to $5,000 per project (typical $500-2,500). Free curriculum + monthly virtual seminars. Past projects: schoolyard rain gardens, climate-action campaigns, beach cleanup data, weather stations. Strong fit for kids interested in environmental science with real-world impact + funding to actually do something.

programs.name: Outdoor Afro Youth + Family Programs

cost.display: FREE for Outdoor Afro participants — chapter-led trips

programs.deadline: Chapter-led trips year-round
programs.description: Outdoor Afro celebrates Black connections + leadership in nature. 60+ city chapters run free hikes, camping trips, paddling, fishing, climbing, and family events. Founded by Rue Mapp. Particularly impactful for Black families historically under-served in outdoor recreation. Chapters in Seattle, Bay Area, Chicago, ATL, NYC, DC, etc. Pairs naturally with NPS Junior Ranger + Sierra Club ICO.

programs.name: Earthwatch Kids + Family Expeditions

cost.display: ~$2,000-3,500/wk + airfare; need-based aid via Ignite Awards (covers up to 100%)

location.city: Field sites worldwide (Costa Rica, Iceland, Kenya, Bahamas, etc.)

programs.deadline: Family expeditions year-round; book 6-8 months ahead
programs.description: Earthwatch Family Expeditions: parents + kids join real scientists on conservation field research. 8-12 day trips to field sites worldwide (sea turtles in Costa Rica, lemurs in Madagascar, climate change in Iceland, Caribbean reefs). Kids ages 8+ accepted with parent. Earthwatch's Ignite Awards provide up to 100% scholarships for qualifying low-income youth. Real science contribution + immersive intl experience. Premium pricing but powerful long-term memory.

programs.name: Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools

cost.display: 100% FREE for participating schools (Special Olympics covers all program costs)

programs.deadline: Year-round school enrollment
programs.description: Special Olympics Unified Champion Schools is the K-12 education program that combines inclusive sports + leadership + whole-school engagement. Three components: (1) Unified Sports — students with and without intellectual disabilities play together, (2) Inclusive Youth Leadership, (3) Whole-School Engagement events. 7,500+ US schools participate. 100% free; Special Olympics provides curriculum, coaching, equipment subsidies. Strongest school-based disability-inclusion program in the US.

programs.name: Easter Seals Camps + Inclusive Recreation

cost.display: Day camps ~$200-500/wk; residential ~$700-1,200/wk; sliding scale + scholarships heavy

programs.deadline: Member registration Jan-Feb; general March-April
programs.description: Easterseals' 70+ US affiliates run summer camps explicitly designed for kids with disabilities — autism, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, physical disability, sensory processing differences. Programs span day camps, residential weeks, family weekends, and parents' respite weekends. Trained staff with 1:1 to 3:1 ratios. Sliding-scale + need-based scholarships. Some affiliates include 'typically developing' siblings. Find your local affiliate via easterseals.com.

programs.name: Camp Korey (chronic illness camp, WA)

cost.display: 100% FREE — including travel + meals + medical care

programs.deadline: Apply 4-6 months before session; sessions disease-specific
programs.description: Camp Korey serves kids with serious medical conditions (cancer, blood disorders, neurological conditions, etc.) FREE including travel, meals, medical care. SeriousFun Network founded by Paul Newman. Disease-specific weeks (e.g., 'cancer week', 'kidney week') so kids share their condition with peers. Full-time medical team on-site. 50-acre site in Carnation WA. Sibling weekends + family retreats also offered. Application via referring physician.

programs.name: Friendship Circle (special needs + peer-buddy program)

cost.display: 100% FREE for participating families with special-needs kids

location.city: 100+ chapters in US, Canada, UK, Israel, France, Brazil, Mexico

programs.deadline: Year-round enrollment
programs.description: Friendship Circle pairs kids/teens with special needs (autism, IDD, physical disabilities) with typical-peer 'buddies' for weekly home visits + monthly group events + summer programs. Buddies are HS volunteers. 100+ chapters globally. 100% FREE for families with special-needs kids. Founded by Chabad-Lubavitch but open to all faiths/none. Strong disability-inclusion + community for families isolated by their kid's needs.

programs.name: AHRC Camps + Recreation
programs.provider: AHRC New York City + AHRC NY State

cost.display: Day camps ~$300-700/wk; residential ~$800-1,200/wk; OPWDD funding covers most for NY residents

location.city: NYC + Westchester + Long Island + upstate NY

programs.deadline: Member registration January; general March
programs.description: AHRC New York runs the largest network of disability-focused camps + recreation in NYC metro. Day camps in all 5 boroughs + residential at Camp Anne (NY upstate). For NY residents, OPWDD (Office for People with Developmental Disabilities) waiver funding covers most costs. Open to autism, IDD, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, sensory processing. 1:1 staffing for kids with significant support needs. Sibling Days + family events.

programs.name: Autism Society Resource Network — local camps + summer programs

cost.display: Varies by local affiliate; Autism Society directory lists state-by-state options + funding

programs.deadline: Affiliate-specific
programs.description: Autism Society of America's 75+ state + local affiliates maintain summer-camp directories specifically vetted for autistic kids. Resources include: (a) autism-specific camps (full immersion), (b) inclusive camps (mainstream camps with autism-trained staff), (c) family camps. Most state affiliates also know which Medicaid HCBS waivers can fund camp + respite care in their state. Best starting point for parents new to autism camp landscape.

programs.name: American Indian Science & Engineering Society (AISES) Pre-College

cost.display: Most programs FREE for Native youth; AISES National Conference travel scholarships available

location.city: Online + 200+ AISES collegiate chapters + Tribal college network

programs.deadline: Year-round; National Conference fall
programs.description: AISES is the leading professional society for Native American/Indigenous people in STEM. Pre-college programs include: Online tutoring + mentorship matching with Native STEM professionals, summer 'Lighting the Pathway' college prep, and access to the AISES National Conference (largest gathering of Indigenous STEM professionals + students annually). Pipeline to AISES college scholarships ($1K-$10K). Open to enrolled tribal members, descendants, and Alaska Natives + Native Hawaiians.

programs.name: Native Like Water (Indigenous youth ocean conservation)

cost.display: FREE for accepted Indigenous youth (donations from Patagonia + others fund operations)

location.city: California coast — Pala, Camp Pendleton area + ocean expeditions

programs.deadline: Summer programs apply Feb-March
programs.description: Native Like Water connects Indigenous youth (Native American, Pacific Islander, Native Hawaiian, Maori, Aboriginal) with ocean + coastal cultural practices. Summer immersion programs include surfing, paddling, free-diving, marine biology, and traditional Indigenous coastal ecological knowledge. 100% free for accepted youth — funded by Patagonia + private donors. Highly selective (~30-40 youth per cohort). One of the strongest cultural-identity + outdoor programs for Indigenous youth in the western US.

programs.name: Camp Brave Trails (LGBTQ+ youth + family)

cost.display: ~$1,400-1,800/wk; sliding-scale + scholarship pool covers ~50% of campers

programs.deadline: Sessions June-August; book by April
programs.description: Camp Brave Trails is the leading summer camp for LGBTQ+ youth ages 12-18. Sessions in California (Angeles National Forest) + Maryland. Affirming community for queer + trans + nonbinary teens with traditional summer-camp activities (hiking, swimming, ropes course, arts) plus identity-supportive programming. Trained queer + trans staff. Sliding scale + scholarship pool covers ~50% of campers. Strong combination of fun + community for kids who may not be out at home.

programs.name: Family Equality Council Family Week

cost.display: Family registration ~$1,200-1,800; scholarship pool covers ~30% of attending families

programs.deadline: Annual gathering early August; register Jan-March
programs.description: Family Equality's Family Week is the largest annual gathering of LGBTQ+ parents + their kids in North America. 1,800+ family members attend each year in Provincetown MA. Programming spans age-banded kids' activities (Tots, Kids, Tweens, Teens), parent workshops, beach time, and community-building. Strong intergenerational queer-family experience — many kids report it as their highlight of the year. Scholarship + travel-grant pools available.

programs.name: Interlochen Arts Camp Junior Programs

cost.display: Junior Division (grades 3-6): ~$3,500-5,500/2 weeks; need-based aid covers 30-100% for ~40% of campers

programs.deadline: Apply Nov-Jan; auditions Feb for performing-arts tracks
programs.description: Interlochen is the most prestigious performing-arts summer camp in the US. Junior Division (grades 3-6) + Intermediate Division (7-9) + High School Division. Tracks: classical music, jazz, dance, theatre, creative writing, film, visual arts. Selective (auditions for performing arts; portfolio for visual). Strong need-based financial aid covers up to 100% — about 40% of campers receive aid. Located on a 1,200-acre campus in Northern Michigan.

programs.name: USA Junior Olympic — multi-sport developmental pipeline
programs.provider: USA Track & Field + USA Swimming + USA Gymnastics + sport-specific NGBs

cost.display: Club registration varies; USATF youth membership ~$30-50/yr; meets ~$15-50 each; many clubs have aid

location.city: Local USATF/USA Swimming/USA Gymnastics clubs nationwide

programs.deadline: Year-round club enrollment; Junior Olympic championships summer
programs.description: Each Olympic-sport National Governing Body (USATF, USA Swimming, USA Gymnastics, USA Wrestling, etc.) operates a Junior Olympic developmental pipeline from local clubs through state, regional, and national championships. Best entry to organized competitive sport for kids beyond rec leagues. Each NGB has its own age divisions, qualifying standards, and scholarship pools. Find local clubs via the NGB website (e.g., usatf.org/youth-clubs).
